text.p: Mexican glass company Vitro SA said its 1996 results were negatively affected by its sale of U.S.-based Anchor Glass Corp. and the reduction of its stake in Mexico's Grupo Financiero Serfin.
Vitro's net loss during 1996 was 3.824 billion pesos versus a profit of 775 million in 1995.

During the fourth quarter alone, Vitro registered profits of 450 million pesos versus a net loss of 552.7 million during the same period of 1995. Its operating profit during the last quarter was 644.6 million pesos versus 800 million pesos during the fourth quarter of the previous year.
Vitro took a 3.672 billion peso charge during the year for its September sale of Anchor Glass and also took a 963.5 million peso charge for the reduction of its stake in Serfin.
The company said it used 1996 as a year to refocus its strategy and divest non-essential assets.
"This has been a year of transition for Vitro...and we have...set out on a clear path to growth," Vitro Director General Federico Sada said in the statement.
"We realise the numbers we just reported are not attractive and that much remains to be done. However, the tough decisions have already been taken...." Sada added.
Vitro's operating cash flow during 1996 was 4.2 billion pesos versus 4.77 billion during the year before. The company said cash flow in dollar terms has been steady at about $500 million.
Vitro's exports grew 9.2 percent during the year to $572.5 million. Its operating margin was 17.3 percent during the year, compared to 20.3 percent the year before.
